posts.title: BREAKING: Geely to take 30% stake in Nio Power with battery swap assets and cash
posts.summary:
Geely will invest its entire equity interest in Yiyi Power and 640 million yuan in cash in Nio Power, integrating battery swap operations for commercial fleets.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Holding will acquire a 30% stake in Nio Power by contributing its Yiyi Power battery swap business and 640 million yuan in cash, valuing Nio Power at 16 billion yuan.
The deal integrates Geely's commercial fleet battery swap operations into Nio Power, marking a significant shift from technical cooperation to full business integration.
Nio China will retain a 63.6% controlling stake in Nio Power, while also acquiring a 10% equity interest in Geely's charging subsidiary, Haohan Energy.
Geely holds an option to invest an additional 640 million yuan within two years, which would increase its stake to 34% and dilute Nio China's holding to 60%.

posts.title: EU presses UK to raise tariffs on Chinese EVs, report says
posts.summary:
The EU links treatment of British goods to closer trade policy alignment and suggests London join its customs union.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The European Union is pressuring the UK to align its trade policy and increase tariffs on Chinese EVs to prevent Britain from becoming a loophole for Chinese goods entering the EU market.
Brussels has suggested that the UK join the EU customs union to resolve trade friction, though the British government has explicitly ruled out this option.

The UK faces a strategic dilemma: raising tariffs could protect its position in European supply chains but risks deterring Chinese automotive investment, such as potential production deals with Chery.
Chinese manufacturers currently hold a 16% share of the UK's new car market, significantly higher than in markets where the EU has already implemented countervailing duties of up to 45.3%.

posts.title: China state media rebuts 'de-CATLization,' warns of battery supply chain price competition
posts.summary:
A media outlet under MIIT says supply chain diversification should not be portrayed as a confrontation between automakers and battery producers.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Chinese state media has issued a commentary criticizing the 'de-CATLization' narrative, warning that aggressive supply chain diversification could undermine industry collaboration and quality standards.
The report cautions that intense price competition in the NEV sector is spreading upstream, potentially forcing battery suppliers to compromise on long-term reliability and technological innovation.

The MIIT-affiliated outlet also criticized automakers for misleading marketing, noting that some companies falsely label system integration or battery pack design as proprietary 'in-house' cell development.

posts.title: Li Auto solid-state battery timeline points to limited vehicle use in 2027 or 2028
posts.summary:
Li Auto has several solid-state battery projects underway and has validated prototypes in eyewear products.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto expects to achieve limited vehicle deployment of solid-state batteries by 2027 or 2028, though full-scale mature mass production remains approximately five years away.
The company is currently addressing significant technical hurdles regarding battery lifespan, charging performance, and cost-efficiency.
Li Auto is deepening its vertical integration through a joint venture with Sunwoda, with plans to become the second-largest shareholder in Sunwoda EVB to secure its battery supply chain.
